endorsements.quote: Models trained on augmented datasets must be tested on real-only external cohorts to detect artefacts introduced by synthetic augmentation.
AI models consuming hybrid real–synthetic data should be evaluated with explicit stratification by data source and clinically relevant subgroups [ 1 – 4 , 19 , 31 , 116 – 118 , 120 – 122 ].

Integrating bias and drift monitoring with such provenance tools—datasheets, synthetic data cards, and model cards—should be considered a core design requirement for virtual-tissue–AI systems rather than an optional post hoc add-on.

For virtual-tissue-informed synthetic cohorts, an analogous practice would be to accompany each dataset with a synthetic data card that records at minimum: (i) the real datasets and time windows used for calibration; (ii) the versioned virtual-tissue and generative models that produced the synthetic samples; (iii) the mixture of synthetic and real data used in training downstream AI components and the contribution of each to performance; (iv) evaluation metrics for fidelity, utility, privacy, and fairness; and (v) intended contexts of use and known limitations.

Ferrara’s analysis of the “butterfly effect” in AI systems further underscores how small initial skews can be amplified through feedback loops, motivating continuous monitoring of both input distributions and subgroup performance with triggers for recalibration or rollback [ 125 ].

unlisted_practices: Evaluate synthetic data as data products for fidelity, downstream utility, and privacy risk rather than assuming validity by construction.
Retain a persistent anchor set of real examples never used for training and cap the synthetic-to-real ratio to prevent model collapse.
Use synthetic data to supplement rather than replace real-world data in AI training.
Maintain machine-readable chain-of-custody documentation linking synthetic data records to the generating mechanistic model version and parameters.
Scale verification and validation rigor to model risk and context of use using risk-informed credibility frameworks such as ASME V&V 40.
Flag large unexplained parameter shifts during recalibration as low-confidence and trigger model review rather than forcing a fit.
Validate that digital twin recalibration completes within the clinical decision window.
Use explainable AI to verify decision boundaries rely on biologically plausible features rather than synthetic generator artifacts.
Control subgroup representation in synthetic data generation and document fairness-enhancing interventions.

screen.reason: This is a position paper and conceptual framework paper proposing hybrid systems (virtual tissue models, synthetic data, and AI) for medical digital twins and adapting governance/validation frameworks.
